headline: PBI takes friend into custody as ex-airman's bike found near Turag River
summary: Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) is questioning a friend of former Flight Lieutenant Tahsif Souri after recovering a motorcycle near the river where his body was found.
details: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has launched a shadow investigation into the death of former Air Force Flight Lieutenant Tahsif Souri, alongside the ongoing Naval Police investigation.
As part of the probe, PBI recovered a motorcycle from the Mazar slum area, approximately 50 yards from the Turag River in Tongi.
Authorities are currently verifying if the motorcycle belongs to Tahsif Souri.
On Thursday night, PBI took Ahmed Shahriar Reza Deep, described as a 'junior friend' of Tahsif, into custody for questioning.
Tahsif's body was recovered from the Turag River in Tongi last Wednesday afternoon after he had been missing since the previous day.
Tahsif's father, Enayetul Karim, has alleged that his son was murdered.
caption:

Authorities are currently verifying if the motorcycle belongs to Tahsif Souri.

Tahsif's body was recovered from the Turag River in Tongi last Wednesday afternoon after he had been missing since the previous day.

Tahsif's father, Enayetul Karim, has alleged that his son was murdered.

headline_marked: UN grants [[Bangladesh 3 more years]] for LDC graduation
headline: UN grants Bangladesh 3 more years for LDC graduation
summary: The UN General Assembly has deferred the graduation of Bangladesh and Nepal from the Least Developed Countries (LDC) group until November 24, 2029.
details: The United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution on Thursday in New York, granting a three-year extension to Bangladesh's graduation from the group of least developed countries (LDCs).
Bangladesh will now continue to enjoy LDC benefits until November 24, 2029, extending the preparatory period originally scheduled to end in 2024, then pushed to 2026 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The decision follows a request from the new BNP-led government, with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman writing to the UN Secretary-General in April to seek personal support for the extension.
As an LDC, Bangladesh currently enjoys duty-free and quota-free access to European export markets, benefits that are expected to change once the country graduates to developing-country status.
Businesses had urged for more time to prepare for the loss of these trade benefits, specifically citing challenges facing the pharmaceutical and readymade garment industries.
Representatives from France, Canada, and Ireland (on behalf of the EU) supported the deferment but stressed the need for Bangladesh to continue its reform agenda.
The resolution was adopted by a voice vote, with the session chaired by Bangladesh Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman.
caption:
Bangladesh gets more time to prepare for a major economic shift. The UN has deferred its LDC graduation by 3 years.

The United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution on Thursday in New York, granting a three-year extension to Bangladesh's graduation from the group of least developed countries (LDCs).

Bangladesh will now continue to enjoy LDC benefits until November 24, 2029, extending the preparatory period originally scheduled to end in 2024, then pushed to 2026 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

The decision follows a request from the new BNP-led government, with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman writing to the UN Secretary-General in April to seek personal support for the extension.

As an LDC, Bangladesh currently enjoys duty-free and quota-free access to European export markets, benefits that are expected to change once the country graduates to developing-country status.

Businesses had urged for more time to prepare for the loss of these trade benefits, specifically citing challenges facing the pharmaceutical and readymade garment industries.

Representatives from France, Canada, and Ireland (on behalf of the EU) supported the deferment but stressed the need for Bangladesh to continue its reform agenda.

The resolution was adopted by a voice vote, with the session chaired by Bangladesh Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman.
